Acceptance evidence

Read-only review of the Calculator project (e008de34-69eb-4fea-9b47-b4c23991b17d), including the requirement notes and the actual contents of both attached files.

Requirement	Concrete evidence	Assessment
Basic arithmetic only	Requirement node custom:885b49ee56b34461b9647842f338d4e0: “just basic calculation operation, not scientific.” Markdown asset custom:10dac7e1ea0f406f81cc7d5528d54893, Scope: “Basic, non-scientific calculator.” Its Calculator surface section specifies addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, decimal input, sign toggle, and related basic controls. SVG asset custom:40b78f251b304df980271da6b5979dc7, <desc>: “A basic calculator interface…” and visible keys are limited to numeric/basic arithmetic controls.	Consistent. The proposal explicitly excludes scientific functions, memory functions, and expression editing unless separately approved.
Windows-like calculator layout	Requirement node custom:1c2c40446a364b5281682ec51c158f53: “calculator like windows style calc.” The Markdown Proposed layout depicts a calculator surface with display and keypad; Responsive behavior specifies a two-column desktop layout and a stacked narrow layout. The SVG shows a desktop calculator card, display, keypad, rounded controls, and a desktop-style application composition.	Broadly consistent visually, but limited proof. The SVG supports a conventional Windows-like desktop-calculator appearance; it does not establish an actual Windows platform target or prove conformity to a specific Windows Calculator design.
Calculation-history column on the right	Requirement node custom:1c02ec290b364b1e82f64c77999adc0c: “history column on right with history calculations.” Markdown Scope says “a right-side calculation history column”; Responsive behavior says calculator controls are on the left and history is on the right. SVG <desc> states “display and keypad on the left and calculation history on the right”; the drawing contains a separate right-hand History card with three calculations.	Consistent. Both documents specify and depict the right-side history column for wide layouts.
Mismatches and limits
No material mismatch found across the three requested requirements.
The “Windows-like” requirement is the least objectively demonstrated. The Markdown records the requirement, and the SVG depicts a desktop-style layout, but a static SVG cannot prove platform support, Windows visual-system compliance, or runtime interaction.
The SVG cannot prove:
arithmetic correctness or calculator state transitions;
keyboard support;
divide-by-zero handling;
decimal validation, repeated-operator behavior, or overflow behavior;
history persistence, newest-first ordering over time, or row-selection behavior;
responsive stacking at narrow widths.
The SVG includes the text “Selecting a row may restore its result,” but this is only a visual annotation, not evidence that the interaction exists.
Intended implementation behavior

The Markdown proposal’s Smallest defensible implementation slice calls for:

A calculator display and basic keypad.
Four arithmetic operators, equals, clear, clear-entry, backspace, sign toggle, and decimal input.
In-memory history rendered newest first, with expression and result per row.
Two-column desktop layout, stacking history below the calculator on narrow screens.
Keyboard support and basic accessible labels.
Verification for normal calculations, divide-by-zero, reset, and history behavior.

It also leaves several decisions explicitly open: whether selecting history restores a result, whether history persists across refreshes or remains session-only, and how very large results overflow. No files or project nodes were modified.
